text:
nina: dropped a microflow for the SLO threshold preview — main asks: histogram granularity control + a suppression calendar for quiet windows. figma: https://figma.com/file/threshold-preview
sam: nice, quick q: does histogram granularity default to auto-bucket or a fixed set?
nina: plan is auto by default with a manual dropdown (1m/5m/15m/1h) for power users. shows tooltip on hover.
priya: tooltip is fine, but ensure the dropdown is reachable via keyboard and has aria-label 'Histogram granularity'. avoid relying only on visual ▲/▼ icons.
jorge: calendar suppression looks handy. current mock shows inline mini-calendar with ranges. concern: keyboard date range selection can be fiddly. can we allow text input for quick ranges like 'next 2 hours'?
nina: yes — adding a freeform input with suggestion chips (2h, 24h, until Monday). chips should be selectable via left/right arrows.
priya: for a11y: chips must be focusable and announce their value when focused. also ensure the calendar has role='application' only if necessary; otherwise use standard date grid with proper roving tabindex.
a11y-bot: recommendation: implement grid role for calendar with aria-selected on day cells. provide instructions via visually-hidden element: 'Use arrow keys to move, space to select range start/end'.
sam: tiny copy nit: the current control label reads 'Suppression window' elsewhere we use 'Quiet window'. prefer consistency.
nina: switching to 'Quiet window' across the flow. good catch.
jorge: about the histogram legend: we currently use color + short labels. on dark mode the mid color blends. suggest adding patterns (dots/stripes) for people with color blindness and increase contrast.
ina: patterns would add visual complexity but solve accessibility. perhaps pattern on hover only?
priya: patterns should be present always for non-color cues — don't hide them on hover. also include textual legend near the graph for screen readers.
a11y-bot: automatic check: color-only encoding fails WCAG for some users. include a second redundant encoding (pattern or shape). also ensure chart is keyboard-navigable with focusable datapoints and descriptive aria-labels like '85% latency breaches at 12:05 UTC'.
sam: another UX question: when user edits threshold, preview should simulate triggered notifications — should we show a sample notification stack for different times of day? that could be noisy.
nina: compromise: add a small 'Simulate' dropdown with presets (offpeak/peak/incident) that updates preview. keep default off.
jorge: simulation presets should be explainable. tiny tooltip under each preset explaining what it simulates.
priya: SR users need to be told when simulation changes the DOM significantly. add a polite live region message 'Preview simulation: incident mode — showing 4 notifications'.
a11y-bot: confirm live region and ensure messages are concise and de-duplicated. also recommend debouncing rapid changes to avoid repeated announcements.
nina: action items recap: 1) rename label to 'Quiet window' 2) add granularity dropdown with keyboard support + aria-label 3) add freeform quiet-window input with suggestion chips, chips keyboard navigable 4) calendar should use grid semantics + visually hidden keyboard instructions 5) legend: add redundant encoding (pattern) + textual SR legend 6) implement 'Simulate' presets with aria-live announcements and debounce. i'll push updated frames and an accessibility checklist in the figma comments by EOD.
sam: i'll add scenarios for Dedicated customers in the brief (they require explicit timezone display for calendars).
jorge: i'll prototype patterned legend variations. priya, can you do a quick a11y pass after i upload?
priya: yep, happy to. small follow-up: include zoom 200% screenshots and high-contrast screenshots in the upload.
a11y-bot: quick reminder: verify focus order when panel opens and that focus returns to the trigger on close.
nina: noted, thanks all. tagging @design-critique for visibility :eyes: (attached: figma frames + initial prototype gif)
